subject: Private Offer drawdown cadence + billing waterfall for Q3 commit
messages:
From: Karen Li <karen.li@acmecloud.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on private offer drawdown cadence and billing waterfall

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement here — we have a couple of follow-ups before we can sign the private offer. Specifically: 

- How does the commit drawdown hit our invoice across months? We’re tied to a quarterly spend cadence and need to reconcile forecast vs usage for our finance team.
- If we exceed the committed tokens mid-quarter, does the overage bill on a separate invoice immediately or as part of the next month?
- Can you provide a billing waterfall or example invoice showing a multi-month drawdown with an applied discount?

We also asked GCP Partner Sales for the marketplace private offer ID but haven’t received the full doc yet. Can you share any templates or a sample billing waterfall for Acme’s $600k Q3 commit?

Appreciate it,
Karen
Karen Li
Head of Procurement, Acme Cloud Solutions
procurement@acmecloud.com

[Attachment: Acme_PO_2026Q3.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com
To: Karen Li <karen.li@acmecloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on private offer drawdown cadence and billing waterfall

Hi Karen — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front:

1) Drawdown cadence: GCP consumes the private offer against the committed amount as usage is invoiced monthly. For example, a $600k quarterly commit will be allocated across the three invoice months based on actual tokens/usage; unused commit does not auto-refund but can be reallocated per contract terms (we can include a clause for limited roll-forward if needed).

2) Overage handling: Overages are billed at the agreed overage rate and show up on the next immediate invoice cycle (i.e., the month after the overage occurs). They do not wait until quarter-end aggregation.

3) Billing waterfall: I’ve attached a sample waterfall spreadsheet and a draft private offer PDF for your finance team to review. The waterfall shows: committed amount, month-to-month allocation, realized usage, applied discounts, and the resulting amount invoiced each month.

I’ll loop in Marissa (our Marketplace lead) to confirm the private offer ID and vanessa for any billing/SLA questions. If you’d like, we can run a short 30-min call next week with GCP Partner Sales on the mechanics.

Next steps:
- Marissa: confirm the private offer ID and share the official Marketplace link.
- Vanessa: confirm whether Redwood can support a 30-day roll-forward on unused commit as a commercial gesture.
- Karen: confirm best times for a 30-min joint call with GCP.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0142

[Attachments: RDW-Acme_PrivateOffer_Draft_20260618.pdf, GCP_billing-waterfall_v1.xlsx]

From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com, Karen Li <karen.li@acmecloud.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on private offer drawdown cadence and billing waterfall

Hi all — adding detail from the Marketplace side. We just received the private offer handle from GCP Partner Sales and I can confirm it’s live in the console: marketplace/privateOffer/PO-ACME-2026-7890.

Important notes:
- The private offer is configured for monthly invoicing with a quarterly committed total. GCP’s backend will decrement the committed balance as invoices are generated.
- There is no automatic crediting back to Acme for unused commit inside the quarter; the contract can include a discretionary roll-forward for one month but that must be explicitly requested and approved by Redwood finance + GCP.
- Overages bill at the negotiated overage rate and appear on the next month’s invoice.

I’ve attached the GCP console link and a sample waterfall populated with Acme’s numbers so your FP&A team can see the line items. Happy to jump on a call with GCP if you want them to walk through an example invoice.

Marissa Cole
Head of Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

From: dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Question on private offer drawdown cadence and billing waterfall

Sergio / Vanessa — forwarding Acme’s procurement questions. Key asks: they want a billing waterfall example for a $600k Q3 private offer and to understand whether we can allow a 30-day roll-forward on unused commit as a commercial concession.

My proposal: offer a one-month roll-forward limited to 10% of the committed amount (commercial credit) to help close the deal. If acceptable, we should get finance sign-off and update the private offer terms before we send the final DocuSign.

Can you weigh in on:
- Whether a 10% one-month roll-forward is available under Redwood pricing policy for enterprise private offers.
- Any SLA/billing implications that would require signoff from Finance or Legal.

Thanks,
Dylan

From: sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Question on private offer drawdown cadence and billing waterfall

Dylan — quick take:

- Commercial concession: Approve a one-time 10% roll-forward on unused commit for Q3 as a closing concession, provided Acme signs the private offer and PO within 7 business days. Finance will need to record it as a contra-revenue allowance tied to Deal RDW-ACME-2026-Q3.
- Billing ops: Vanessa — please confirm operational steps for flagging the private offer so GCP applies the roll-forward on the first invoice after quarter-end. We should also add a line in the private offer terms documenting the discretionary roll-forward.
- Legal: I’ll ask Legal to add the clause for a one-month 10% roll-forward and include the approval condition.

Sergio Alvarez
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com

[Inline: approval note for finance & legal follow-up]

I’ve attached an updated draft private offer reflecting the roll-forward clause and an updated billing waterfall example populated with Acme’s numbers (we applied the concession to month 3).
